source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֔ע לְדָרְיָ֖וֶשׁ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָ֗ה בְּאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁעִ֖י בְּכִסְלֵֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in year four of Darius the king, came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah, on the fourth of the month the ninth, in Kislev.

en.L: And it came about in the fourth year of Darius the king that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah on the fourth of the ninth month, in Kislev.
en.B: In the fourth year of King Darius's reign, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah. It was the fourth day of Kislev, the ninth month.
en.R: In Darius's fourth year as king, on the fourth day of Kislev, the ninth month of the year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message to Zechariah.

pt.L: E aconteceu no quarto ano do rei Dario [que] a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias, no quarto [dia] do nono mês, em Quisleu.
pt.B: No quarto ano do rei Dario, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias. Era o quarto dia de Quisleu, o nono mês.
pt.R: No quarto ano em que Dario era rei, no dia quatro de Quisleu, o nono mês do ano, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu uma mensagem a Zacarias.

decisions.choice: the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev, in Darius's fourth year: early December 518 BC
decisions.reason: This is nearly two years after the night visions (1:7) and about halfway through the rebuilding of the temple, which was finished in Darius's sixth year (Ezra 6:15). Kislev is the Babylonian name of the ninth month, used also in Nehemiah 1:1. The modern date is worked out from the Babylonian calendar.

decisions.choice: Zechariah is named in the third person
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 1:7, a heading speaks of the prophet by name. Chapters 7-8 hold the prophet's answer to a question about fasting, given in several messages (7:4, 8; 8:1, 18).

decisions.choice: in the fourth year of Darius the king (L); of King Darius's reign (B); in Darius's fourth year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The dated heading follows the wording of 1:1 at each level. Here the Hebrew calls Darius "the king". Readable puts the date first and says "of the year" for the month, without converting to the modern calendar.

decisions.choice: the dated heading of 1:1 and 1:7; o rei Dario; Quisleu
decisions.reason: The heading keeps the wording 1:1 sets at each level, with "o rei Dario" where the Hebrew calls him king, as Haggai 1:1 has it in Portuguese (r-en-1). The month (m1) is "Quisleu", the form Nehemiah 1:1 has in Portuguese.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל שַׂר־אֶ֕צֶר וְרֶ֥גֶם מֶ֖לֶךְ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֑יו לְחַלּ֖וֹת אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Bethel Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to entreat the face of Yahweh,

en.L: And Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to entreat the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to seek the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: The people of the town of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to be kind to them.

pt.L: E Betel enviou Sarezer e Regém-Meleque e os seus homens para suplicar o favor {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}},
pt.B: O povo de Betel tinha enviado Sarezer e Regém-Meleque com os seus homens para buscar o favor {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}
pt.R: O povo da cidade de Betel tinha enviado Sarezer e Regém-Meleque, com os homens deles, para pedir {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} que fosse bondoso com eles.

decisions.choice: Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech: the town of Bethel sent two men with their companions
alternatives: Bethel-sharezer sent Regem-melech and his men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in more than one way. Bethel may be the subject, the town standing for its people, as cities often do. Or "Bethel-sharezer" may be one man's name, a Babylonian-style name formed with the name of a god, and he sent Regem-melech. A few take Bethel as the place to which the men were sent, but the question is put to the priests of the temple in Jerusalem (verse 3). The translation takes the first reading.

decisions.choice: Bethel: a town north of Jerusalem, resettled after the exile; Sharezer: a Babylonian name
decisions.reason: Bethel lay about twelve miles north of Jerusalem, and people of Bethel were among those who returned (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32). Sharezer is a name of Babylonian form (compare 2 Kings 19:37), and Regem-melech may mean "friend of the king"; such names suggest men born in the exile.

decisions.choice: to entreat the favor of the LORD: to pray to the LORD and seek his goodwill
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "to soften the face", means to seek someone's favor (Exodus 32:11; Malachi 1:9). The delegation comes to worship and to ask a question.

decisions.choice: The people of Bethel (B, R); their men (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of" for the town, as m1 reads it, and "their men" for the companions of the two. Readable says what entreating the LORD's favor means. The sentence runs on into verse 3, so Literal ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: Betel; Sarezer; Regém-Meleque
decisions.reason: The names (m2) take the forms Portuguese gives them: "Betel" as Genesis 28:19, "Sarezer" as Isaiah 37:38, and "Regém-Meleque" with "Meleque" as in "Ebede-Meleque" (Jeremiah 38:7).

source.text: לֵאמֹ֗ר אֶל־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְבֵית־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֶל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הַֽאֶבְכֶּה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִשִׁ֔י הִנָּזֵ֕ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי זֶ֖ה כַּמֶּ֥ה שָׁנִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: saying to the priests who [belong] to [the] house of Yahweh of hosts and to the prophets, saying, Shall I weep in the month the fifth, separating myself, as I have done these how many years?

en.L: saying to the priests of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts and to the prophets, "Should I weep in the fifth month, keeping myself apart, as I have done for how many years now?"
en.B: and to ask the priests of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies and the prophets, "Should I go on weeping and fasting in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?"
en.R: They were to ask the priests of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies and the prophets, "Should we keep on mourning and fasting in the fifth month, as we have done for so many years?"

pt.L: dizendo aos sacerdotes da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos e aos profetas: "Devo chorar no quinto mês, mantendo-me separado, como tenho feito há tantos anos?"
pt.B: e perguntar aos sacerdotes da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos e aos profetas: "Devo continuar chorando e jejuando no quinto mês, como tenho feito há tantos anos?"
pt.R: Eles deviam perguntar aos sacerdotes do templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos e aos profetas: "Devemos continuar a fazer luto e jejum no quinto mês, como fazemos há tantos anos?"

decisions.choice: the fifth month: the fast that mourned the burning of the temple
decisions.reason: In the fifth month of 586 BC, the Babylonian commander burned the temple, the king's palace and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-9; Jeremiah 52:12-13). The exiles mourned the day with a fast. Now that the temple was being rebuilt, the people of Bethel asked whether the fast should go on. The answer comes at the end of chapter 8 (8:19), after the LORD has spoken about the heart of the matter.

decisions.choice: keeping myself apart: abstaining, keeping a fast
decisions.reason: The verb means to set oneself apart, and is related to the word for a Nazirite, who abstained from wine (Numbers 6:2-3). Here it means holding back from food and pleasures in mourning.

decisions.choice: I: the town speaks as one person
decisions.reason: The delegation speaks for the people of Bethel, using "I" for the whole community, as Israel often does in the psalms.

decisions.choice: we (R); mourning and fasting (B, R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "we", since the whole community asks. Balanced and Readable give "keeping myself apart" as "fasting" (m2), and "weep" as "weeping" (B) or "mourning" (R). The priests "who belong to" the house are the priests "of" the house.

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh of hosts to me, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts came to me, saying:
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies came to me:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies gave me this message:

pt.L: E a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: Então a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos veio a mim:
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer begins with a question of his own
decisions.reason: The LORD does not answer the question about the fast at once. He asks whether the fasting was ever for him (verses 5-7), and reminds the people of what the earlier prophets said (verses 8-14). The direct answer comes in 8:18-19.

decisions.choice: the formula with "the LORD of hosts"
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for "the word of the LORD came to me", with "of hosts" at Literal and "of Armies" at the other levels.

source.text: אֱמֹר֙ אֶל־כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּֽי־צַמְתֶּ֨ם וְסָפ֜וֹד בַּחֲמִישִׁ֣י וּבַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וְזֶה֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה הֲצ֥וֹם צַמְתֻּ֖נִי אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to all [the] people of the land and to the priests, saying, When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh, and this seventy years, did you really fast for me, me?

en.L: Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth [month] and in the seventh, these seventy years, was it really for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that you fasted, for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and the seventh months for these seventy years, did you truly fast for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Tell all the people of the land and the priests, "For seventy years you have fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh month. But were you really fasting for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

pt.L: Dize a todo o povo da terra e aos sacerdotes: "Quando vocês jejuaram e prantearam no quinto [mês] e no sétimo, estes setenta anos, foi realmente por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} que jejuaram, por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}?
pt.B: Dize a todo o povo da terra e aos sacerdotes: "Quando vocês jejuaram e prantearam no quinto e no sétimo mês durante estes setenta anos, foi de fato por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} que jejuaram?
pt.R: Diz a todo o povo da terra e aos sacerdotes: "Durante setenta anos vocês jejuaram e fizeram luto no quinto mês e no sétimo mês. Mas será que vocês estavam mesmo jejuando por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}?

decisions.choice: the seventh month: the fast that mourned the murder of Gedaliah
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition connects a fast in the seventh month with the murder of Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians set over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem; his death drove the last of the people to Egypt (2 Kings 25:25-26; Jeremiah 41:1-3). The Day of Atonement also falls in the seventh month (Leviticus 16:29), but it was commanded in the law, and the fasts here are fasts of mourning added in the exile. The connection with Gedaliah is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: these seventy years: since the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: From 586 BC to this message in 518 BC was nearly seventy years, the time of judgment foretold by Jeremiah; see the note at 1:12.

decisions.choice: was it really for me: a question about motive, stressed by repeating "me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the pronoun at the end, "for me, me?" The LORD asks whether their fasting was turned toward him, or was only grief for their own loss. Isaiah 58:3-7 asks the same of fasting without justice.

decisions.choice: for me ... for me (L); did you truly fast for me (B); were you really fasting for me (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun; Balanced and Readable show the stress with "truly" and "really". "Me" takes the setting for pronouns of God. The words Zechariah is to say are in double quotation marks, which close at the end of verse 7. Readable makes the long question a statement and a short question.

source.text: וְכִ֥י תֹאכְל֖וּ וְכִ֣י תִשְׁתּ֑וּ הֲל֤וֹא אַתֶּם֙ הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים וְאַתֶּ֖ם הַשֹּׁתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And when you eat and when you drink, [are] not you the ones eating, and you the ones drinking?

en.L: And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who eat and you who drink?
en.B: And when you eat and drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?
en.R: And when you eat and drink, are you not doing it just for yourselves?

pt.L: E quando vocês comem e quando bebem, não são vocês que comem e vocês que bebem?
pt.B: E, quando vocês comem e bebem, não é para vocês mesmos que comem e bebem?
pt.R: E, quando vocês comem e bebem, não fazem isso só para vocês mesmos?

decisions.choice: is it not you who eat and you who drink: your feasting, like your fasting, is for yourselves
decisions.reason: The stress falls on "you". Whether they fast or feast, the people are thinking of themselves, not of the LORD. Religion that serves only the worshiper is empty.

decisions.choice: for yourselves (B); just for yourselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stressed "you" means.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֔ים בִּהְי֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת וּשְׁלֵוָ֔ה וְעָרֶ֖יהָ סְבִיבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְהַנֶּ֥גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה יֹשֵֽׁב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [Are] not the words which proclaimed Yahweh by [the] hand of the prophets the former, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah inhabited?

en.L: Are not [these] the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed by the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah were inhabited?"
en.B: Are these not the very words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, along with the towns around it, and when people lived in the Negev and the Shephelah?"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke these same words through the prophets of long ago. At that time people lived in Jerusalem, and it was doing well. People lived in the towns around it, in the Negev in the south and in the western foothills."

pt.L: Não [são estas] as palavras que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} proclamou por meio dos profetas antigos, quando Jerusalém era habitada e tranquila, e as suas cidades ao seu redor, e o Neguebe e a Sefelá eram habitados?"
pt.B: Não são estas as mesmas palavras que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} proclamou por meio dos profetas de antigamente, quando Jerusalém era habitada e próspera, junto com as cidades ao redor, e quando havia gente morando no Neguebe e nas colinas do oeste?"
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} falou estas mesmas palavras por meio dos profetas de muito tempo atrás. Naquele tempo havia gente morando em Jerusalém, e a cidade ia bem. Havia gente morando nas cidades ao redor dela, no Neguebe, no sul, e nas colinas do oeste."

decisions.choice: are not these the words: the former prophets said the same
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "are not the words", leaving "these" to be understood. The LORD points to what the earlier prophets said about fasting and worship without justice (Isaiah 58:3-7; Jeremiah 14:12), which verses 9-10 sum up.

decisions.choice: at ease: safe and prosperous
decisions.reason: The word describes a settled, peaceful life (Jeremiah 49:31; Psalm 122:6-7). The prophets spoke when the land was full and thriving, and it was lost because the people did not listen.

decisions.choice: the Negev and the Shephelah: the dry south and the low hills to the west
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry country south of Judah's hills; the Shephelah is the band of low hills between the hill country and the coastal plain. With Jerusalem and its towns, they make up the whole of Judah.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question (R); in the south; the western foothills (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means, and says where the Negev and the Shephelah were. The closing mark ends the words begun in verse 5.

decisions.choice: o Neguebe; a Sefelá (L), as colinas do oeste (B, R)
decisions.reason: The regions (m3) take the wording Jeremiah 17:26 has in Portuguese: "o Neguebe" at every level, and "a Sefelá" at Literal, where Balanced and Readable say where it lies, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Zechariah, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah, saying:
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Zechariah this message:

pt.L: E a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias, dizendo:
pt.B: Então a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a Zacarias:
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu a Zacarias esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: a further word: what the former prophets said, and what came of it
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 sum up the message of the earlier prophets, which still stands, and verses 11-14 tell how the ancestors refused it and were scattered.

decisions.choice: the formula with Zechariah's name
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for the prophets, with the prophet named in place of "me".

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ שְׁפֹ֔טוּ וְחֶ֣סֶד וְרַֽחֲמִ֔ים עֲשׂ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: Justice of truth judge, and loyal love and compassion do, each with his brother,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion {{gender:toward one another|each man toward his brother}};
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Judge with true justice. Show loyal love and compassion to one another.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Judge fairly and honestly. Show faithful love and compassion to one another.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Julguem com juízo de verdade, e pratiquem o amor leal e a compaixão {{gender:uns com os outros|cada um com o seu irmão}};
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: Julguem com verdade. Mostrem amor leal e compaixão uns pelos outros.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: Julguem com justiça e honestidade. Mostrem amor fiel e compaixão uns pelos outros.

decisions.choice: judge with true justice: give verdicts that are fair and can be trusted
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to all who settle disputes, from judges to elders at the town gate. "True" means faithful and reliable, a judgment that does not bend for a bribe or for the powerful (Ezekiel 18:8).

decisions.choice: loyal love and compassion: faithful kindness and tender mercy toward others
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the loyal love that people bound together owe one another (see the note at Hosea 6:6). The second word is the compassion of a parent for a child (Psalm 103:13). The LORD asks his people to treat one another as he treats them.

decisions.choice: the message of the earlier prophets in a few words
decisions.reason: Justice, loyal love and care for the weak are the heart of the earlier prophets' call (Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8; Jeremiah 7:5-6; 22:3). This, not fasting, is what the LORD asked.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); toward one another / each man toward his brother (L)
decisions.reason: *Hesed* follows the settled wording for the prophets. "Each man toward his brother" means everyone toward everyone, men and women alike, so Literal gives it the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "one another". The sentence runs on into verse 10, so Literal ends with a semicolon.

decisions.choice: Julguem com juízo de verdade (L); Julguem com verdade (B); Julguem com justiça e honestidade (R); amor leal (L, B), amor fiel (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb with its own noun, "julgar com juízo"; Balanced says "Julguem com verdade", a verdict that can be trusted (m1); Readable says it in two plain words. Hesed is "amor leal" (L, B) and "amor fiel" (R), the wording set for the prophets.

decisions.choice: uns com os outros / cada um com o seu irmão (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the phrase means everyone toward everyone, so Literal puts it under the gender setting, with "uns com os outros" as the inclusive default and the Hebrew picture as the alternative; "uns pelos outros" at Balanced and Readable is already inclusive.

source.text: וְאַלְמָנָ֧ה וְיָת֛וֹם גֵּ֥ר וְעָנִ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲשֹׁ֑קוּ וְרָעַת֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אַֽל־תַּחְשְׁב֖וּ בִּלְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and widow and fatherless, sojourner and poor, do not oppress, and evil of each [against] his brother do not plan in your heart.

en.L: and do not oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor; and do not devise evil in your hearts {{gender:against one another|each man against his brother}}.
en.B: Do not oppress the widow or the orphan, the outsider or the poor. And do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
en.R: Do not mistreat widows, orphans, foreigners or poor people. Do not even think about how to harm one another.

pt.L: e não oprimam a viúva e o órfão, o imigrante e o pobre; e não planejem o mal no coração de vocês {{gender:uns contra os outros|cada um contra o seu irmão}}.
pt.B: Não oprimam a viúva nem o órfão, o imigrante nem o pobre. E não tramem o mal no coração de vocês uns contra os outros.
pt.R: Não maltratem as viúvas, as crianças que perderam o pai, os imigrantes nem os pobres. Nem pensem em fazer mal uns aos outros.

decisions.choice: the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor: people with no one to protect them
decisions.reason: The law and the prophets name these four again and again (Exodus 22:20-23; Deuteronomy 24:17; Jeremiah 7:6; 22:3). A widow and a fatherless child had lost the man who stood up for them; a sojourner was a foreigner living in Israel without land or family; the poor had nothing to fall back on.

decisions.choice: devise evil in your hearts: plot harm in secret
decisions.reason: The "heart" is where plans are made. The command reaches behind deeds to intentions, which only God sees. 8:17 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the fatherless, the sojourner (L); the orphan, the outsider (B); orphans, foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: The words for the fatherless and the sojourner follow Jeremiah 22:3 at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "foreigners", the plainest word for someone living away from their own people. "Against one another" takes the gender setting at Literal, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: a viúva, o órfão, o imigrante (L, B); as viúvas, as crianças que perderam o pai, os imigrantes (R)
decisions.reason: The four (m1) keep the words Jeremiah 7:6 and 22:3 set in Portuguese: "o imigrante, o órfão e a viúva" at Literal and Balanced, and "as crianças que perderam o pai" at Readable. The ger is "o imigrante" at every level, where the English Readable says "foreigners", since Portuguese keeps one word for him through the prophets.

source.text: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֔יב וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ כָתֵ֖ף סֹרָ֑רֶת וְאָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם הִכְבִּ֥ידוּ מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they refused to pay attention, and they gave a shoulder stubborn, and their ears they made heavy from hearing.

en.L: But they refused to pay attention, and they turned a stubborn shoulder, and they made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
en.B: But they refused to pay attention. They turned their shoulders away stubbornly and stopped up their ears so that they would not hear.
en.R: But your ancestors refused to listen. They stubbornly turned away and covered their ears so they could not hear.

pt.L: Mas eles se recusaram a prestar atenção, e deram um ombro rebelde, e tornaram pesados os seus ouvidos para não ouvir.
pt.B: Mas eles se recusaram a prestar atenção. Viraram o ombro com teimosia e taparam os ouvidos para não ouvir.
pt.R: Mas os antepassados de vocês não quiseram escutar. Viraram as costas com teimosia e taparam os ouvidos para não ouvir.

decisions.choice: a stubborn shoulder: like an ox that will not take the yoke
decisions.reason: The picture is of an animal pulling its shoulder away from the yoke (Nehemiah 9:29; Hosea 4:16). The ancestors would not submit to the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: they made their ears heavy: they made themselves deaf
decisions.reason: "Heavy" ears are ears that will not hear (Isaiah 6:10). The people chose not to listen.

decisions.choice: they: the ancestors, who heard the earlier prophets
decisions.reason: The verse continues the story of the generations before the exile, whose refusal led to their scattering (verse 14; compare 1:4).

decisions.choice: your ancestors (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: deram um ombro rebelde (L); viraram o ombro (B); viraram as costas (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the ox pulling its shoulder from the yoke (m1); Balanced keeps "ombro" with a verb Portuguese uses for turning away; Readable says "viraram as costas", the Portuguese idiom for refusing someone.

source.text: וְלִבָּ֞ם שָׂ֣מוּ שָׁמִ֗יר מִ֠שְּׁמוֹעַ אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בְּרוּח֔וֹ בְּיַ֖ד הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי֙ קֶ֣צֶף גָּד֔וֹל מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And their heart they made diamond from hearing the instruction and the words which sent Yahweh of hosts by his Spirit by [the] hand of the prophets the former; and there was wrath great from Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And they made their hearts [like] diamond, so as not to hear the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit by the hand of the former prophets; and great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: They made their hearts as hard as diamond so that they would not listen to the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: They made their hearts as hard as rock so they would not listen to the teaching and the messages that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the prophets of long ago. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies became very angry.

pt.L: E fizeram o seu coração [como] diamante, para não ouvirem a instrução e as palavras que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos enviou pelo {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Espírito por meio dos profetas antigos; e veio grande ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.B: Fizeram o coração duro como diamante, para não ouvirem a instrução e as palavras que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos tinha enviado pelo {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Espírito por meio dos profetas de antigamente. Por isso veio grande ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.R: Eles fizeram o coração ficar duro como pedra, para não escutarem o ensino e as mensagens que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos tinha enviado pelo {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Espírito por meio dos profetas de muito tempo atrás. Por isso {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos ficou muito irado.

decisions.choice: diamond: the hardest stone
decisions.reason: The word names a very hard stone, used as the point of an engraving tool (Jeremiah 17:1) and as a picture of a hard forehead (Ezekiel 3:9). Whether it was diamond, emery or flint, the point is the same: their hearts could not be marked.

decisions.choice: the instruction: God's law and teaching
decisions.reason: The word is *torah*, God's instruction, which the prophets called the people back to.

decisions.choice: by his Spirit through the former prophets: the prophets spoke by God's Spirit
decisions.reason: The words the prophets spoke were sent by the LORD through his Spirit. Nehemiah 9:30 says the same: "you warned them by your Spirit through your prophets."

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R); Spirit, capitalized; as hard as rock (R)
decisions.reason: *Torah* follows the wording set in Isaiah. The Spirit is God's Spirit, so it is capitalized, and "his" takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable says "rock", a common picture of hardness.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י כַאֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֖א וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כֵּ֤ן יִקְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֔ע אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, just as he called and not they listened, so they will call and not I will listen, says Yahweh of hosts,

en.L: And just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to them, but they would not listen. So when they called out, I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

pt.L: E assim como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chamou e eles não ouviram, assim eles chamaram e eu não ouvi, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.B: Assim como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chamou e eles não quiseram ouvir, assim também eles chamaram e eu não quis ouvir, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} chamou o povo, mas eles não quiseram escutar. Por isso, quando eles clamaram, eu não quis escutar, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.

decisions.choice: he called ... I would not listen: the prophet's words become the LORD's own
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking of the LORD as "he" and ends with the LORD speaking as "I". Prophets often move from one to the other, because they speak for him.

decisions.choice: they would not listen, so I would not listen: the people received what they had given
decisions.reason: The same warning is in Proverbs 1:24-28, Jeremiah 11:11 and Micah 3:4: those who refuse to hear God's call will find that he does not answer their cry in the day of trouble.

decisions.choice: they called: in their distress, when disaster came
decisions.reason: The verb form often looks to the future, but here it tells what used to happen, as the story of the past goes on into verse 14.

decisions.choice: he, with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: "He" is the LORD, so it takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable names the LORD at the start to make the change of speaker clear.

source.text: וְאֵ֣סָעֲרֵ֗ם עַ֤ל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּם וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ נָשַׁ֣מָּה אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם מֵֽעֹבֵ֖ר וּמִשָּׁ֑ב וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶֽרֶץ־חֶמְדָּ֖ה לְשַׁמָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I stormed them away among all the nations whom not they had known, and the land was desolate behind them, from passing through and from returning; and they made a land of delight into a desolation.

en.L: And I scattered them with a storm among all the nations whom they had not known; and the land behind them was left desolate, with no one coming or going; and they made the pleasant land a desolation.
en.B: I scattered them like a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land they left behind was so desolate that no one came or went. They turned the pleasant land into a wasteland.
en.R: I scattered them like a storm scatters things, among nations they had never known. The land they left behind became so empty that no one came or went. They turned that beautiful land into a desert.

pt.L: E eu os espalhei com uma tempestade entre todas as nações que eles não tinham conhecido; e a terra ficou desolada atrás deles, sem ninguém que passasse ou voltasse; e eles fizeram da terra agradável uma desolação.
pt.B: Eu os espalhei como um redemoinho entre todas as nações que eles não conheciam. A terra que deixaram para trás ficou tão desolada que ninguém ia nem vinha. Eles transformaram a terra agradável num lugar arrasado.
pt.R: Eu os espalhei como uma tempestade espalha as coisas, entre nações que eles nunca tinham conhecido. A terra que eles deixaram para trás ficou tão vazia que ninguém passava por ali. Eles transformaram aquela terra bonita num deserto.

decisions.choice: I scattered them with a storm: drove them away as a whirlwind blows things away
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a storm or whirlwind (Habakkuk 3:14). The exile swept the people away suddenly and far.

decisions.choice: with no one coming or going: no traffic at all
decisions.reason: "Passing through and returning" means people traveling back and forth. The land was empty of all travelers (Ezekiel 35:7).

decisions.choice: the pleasant land: the land God gave as a treasure
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Jeremiah 3:19 ("a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage") and Psalm 106:24. The people's own sin turned the land of delight into a wasteland. Chapter 8 turns from this past to the promise of what the LORD will now do.

decisions.choice: like a whirlwind (B); like a storm scatters things (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the picture in the verb into a comparison. "Pleasant land" (L, B) becomes "beautiful land" (R).
